newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower but support intact.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower but support intact.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices ended lower Wednesday but with support intact, as the market drifted within the previous day's trading range, dealers said.
Traders said disappointment over a lack of follow-through buying from commodity funds cast a bearish tone over the market, confining prices to negative territory for most of the session.
A late sell-off by day traders pushed prices lower, with renewed selling from the industry accelerating the downtrend.
"We ran into some overhead selling just below yesterday's highs," one broker said. "The funds were buyers yesterday, but we're not seeing any sign of it today."
March futures fell 0.09 cent a lb, to 10.87 cents, having traded form 10.85 to 10.97. May futures eased 0.11, to 10.94, while the outer months slipped 0.06 to 0.08.
The day's volume was estimated at 10,552 lots.
With little physical offtake to give the market impetus, traders said March would have a tough time retesting its recent high of 11.12 cents.

A lower opening on Thursday would position the market for a test of support at 10.80 basis March, with 10.75-10.70 seen as the next key target. To the upside, March would need to clear 10.97-10.98 to attract fresh buying. Additional hurdles were seen at 11.00 and 11.15 cents.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
